topicName: Islamic Family Law: Marriage and Divorce
description: This topic examines Islamic family law, covering the importance of the family, the meaning, pillars and conditions of a valid marriage (nikah), the rights and duties of spouses, forbidden marriages, polygyny and its conditions, and divorce (talaq), iddah and reconciliation.

mcq.questionText: What is the Arabic word commonly used for marriage in Islam?
mcq.explanation: Nikah is the Arabic term for the marriage contract in Islam, while talaq means divorce, iddah is the waiting period, and mahram refers to relatives one may not marry.

mcq.questionText: In Islam, the family is regarded as the basic unit of which larger structure?
mcq.explanation: The family is the foundation of society and the wider Muslim community (ummah); a strong society is built upon stable and righteous families.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is the gift given by the husband to the wife as a right in marriage?
mcq.explanation: The mahr (also called sadaq) is the obligatory marriage gift given by the husband to the wife; it becomes her own property and is a pillar of the marriage.

mcq.questionText: Who is the wali in an Islamic marriage?

options.text: The guardian who gives the bride in marriage
The person who recites the Qur'an at the wedding
The man who pays the mahr

mcq.explanation: The wali is the guardian of the bride, usually her father or nearest male relative, who represents her and consents to the marriage on her behalf.

mcq.questionText: How many witnesses are normally required for a valid Islamic marriage contract?
mcq.explanation: A valid nikah requires at least two upright (trustworthy) witnesses so that the marriage is publicly known and the rights of both parties are protected.

mcq.questionText: The offer (ijab) and acceptance (qabul) in a marriage refer to:

options.text: The proposal of marriage and its acceptance between the two parties
The reading of the marriage sermon

mcq.explanation: Ijab is the offer of marriage and qabul is its acceptance; this clear offer and acceptance is a pillar of the nikah contract.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is NOT one of the purposes of marriage in Islam?

options.text: To find tranquillity, love and mercy between spouses
To continue the human race through lawful children
To protect chastity and avoid sin
To gain wealth and worldly status only

mcq.explanation: Marriage aims at tranquillity, love, lawful children and the protection of chastity; seeking wealth and status alone is not a true Islamic purpose of marriage.

mcq.questionText: Which of these women is a mahram whom a man is permanently forbidden to marry?
mcq.explanation: A man's mother, daughter, sister, aunts and certain other close relatives are mahram, meaning marriage to them is permanently forbidden. A cousin may be married.

mcq.questionText: What is the maximum number of wives a Muslim man may have at one time according to mainstream Sunni teaching?
mcq.explanation: The Qur'an permits a man to marry up to four wives, on the firm condition that he treats them all justly and equally.

mcq.questionText: Polygyny in Islam is permitted only on which key condition?

options.text: That the husband can deal justly and equally between his wives
That all wives are from the same family
That the first wife chooses the second wife

mcq.explanation: The Qur'an permits more than one wife only if the husband can be just and fair to each one in maintenance, time and treatment; if he fears he cannot, he should marry only one.

mcq.questionText: Divorce (talaq) is described in a famous hadith as:

options.text: An act of worship encouraged for all
The most disliked of the permissible things to Allah

mcq.explanation: Although divorce is lawful, it is reported in hadith to be the most disliked of permitted things to Allah, showing it should be a last resort.

options.text: The waiting period a woman observes after divorce or her husband's death

mcq.explanation: Iddah is the prescribed waiting period after divorce or widowhood, during which a woman does not remarry; it confirms whether she is pregnant and allows time for reconciliation.

mcq.questionText: When a wife seeks separation by returning the mahr or agreed payment to the husband, this is called:
mcq.explanation: Khul' is a form of separation initiated by the wife, usually by returning the dowry, when she can no longer continue the marriage.

mcq.questionText: What does Islam encourage spouses to attempt before resorting to divorce?

options.text: Reconciliation, advice and arbitration by family

mcq.explanation: The Qur'an encourages reconciliation, patience and the appointment of arbiters from both families to resolve disputes before any divorce takes place.

mcq.questionText: According to Islamic teaching, who is primarily responsible for the financial maintenance (nafaqah) of the family?
mcq.explanation: The husband is obliged to provide maintenance (nafaqah), including food, clothing and shelter, for his wife and children according to his means.

fib.questionText: The Arabic term for the marriage contract in Islam is _____.
fib.explanation: Nikah is the lawful marriage contract that joins a man and woman in a relationship sanctioned by Islam.

fib.questionText: The obligatory marriage gift given by the husband to the wife is called the _____.
fib.explanation: The mahr (dowry) is a right of the wife and becomes her own property; it is one of the conditions of a valid marriage.

fib.questionText: The guardian who gives the bride in marriage is known as the _____.
fib.explanation: The wali is usually the father or nearest male relative who represents and consents on behalf of the bride.

fib.questionText: A valid marriage contract requires at least _____ upright witnesses.
fib.explanation: Two trustworthy witnesses are required so that the marriage is made public and the rights of both parties are protected.

fib.questionText: The proposal of marriage is called ijab and its acceptance is called _____.
fib.explanation: Ijab (offer) and qabul (acceptance) together form the agreement at the heart of the nikah contract.

fib.questionText: The waiting period observed by a woman after divorce or the death of her husband is called the _____.
fib.explanation: The iddah confirms whether the woman is pregnant and provides time for possible reconciliation before she may remarry.

fib.questionText: Close relatives whom a person is permanently forbidden to marry are called _____ relations.
fib.explanation: Mahram relations, such as one's mother, daughter and sister, can never be married.

fib.questionText: The Arabic word for divorce in Islam is _____.
fib.explanation: Talaq is the dissolution of marriage initiated by the husband and is regarded as a last resort.

fib.questionText: When a wife seeks separation by returning the dowry to her husband, this is called _____.
fib.explanation: Khul' is a separation initiated by the wife, typically by giving back the mahr she received.

fib.questionText: The financial maintenance that a husband must provide for his family is called _____.
fib.explanation: Nafaqah includes food, clothing and shelter, and is the husband's duty according to his ability.

tf.questionText: In Islam, the family is considered the basic building block of society.
tf.explanation: Islam teaches that a healthy society depends on stable, righteous families, making the family its foundational unit.

tf.questionText: The consent of both the bride and the groom is required for a valid Islamic marriage.
tf.explanation: A marriage forced upon either party without genuine consent is not valid; both must freely agree.

tf.questionText: The mahr (dowry) belongs to the bride's father, not to the bride.
tf.explanation: The mahr is the personal property of the wife herself; no one else has a right to take it from her.

tf.questionText: A Muslim man may marry his own sister if she agrees.
tf.explanation: A sister is a mahram, so marriage to her is permanently forbidden regardless of consent.

tf.questionText: Islam allows a man to marry up to four wives only if he can treat them all justly.
tf.explanation: Polygyny is permitted up to four wives on the strict condition of justice and equal treatment among them.

tf.questionText: Divorce is encouraged in Islam as a normal and praiseworthy action.
tf.explanation: Although lawful, divorce is the most disliked of permitted things and should only be used as a last resort.

tf.questionText: A divorced or widowed woman must observe the iddah before she may remarry.
tf.explanation: The iddah is a required waiting period that follows divorce or the death of a husband.

tf.questionText: Khul' is a form of separation that can be initiated by the wife.
tf.explanation: In khul', the wife seeks the dissolution of the marriage, usually by returning the dowry to her husband.

tf.questionText: Islam encourages family arbitration and reconciliation before divorce takes place.
tf.explanation: The Qur'an instructs that arbiters from both families try to reconcile the couple before any separation.

tf.questionText: After divorce, parents have no responsibility for the care and upbringing of their children.
tf.explanation: Both parents remain responsible for the welfare, maintenance and upbringing of their children even after divorce.

summary.questionText: State why the family is important in Islam.
summary.correctAnswer: The family is the basic unit of society where children are raised in faith and good character, providing love, protection and stability for the whole community.
summary.explanation: Islam builds a sound society upon strong families that nurture righteous, well-mannered believers.

summary.questionText: Define nikah and state its ruling.
summary.correctAnswer: Nikah is the lawful marriage contract between a man and woman; it is generally recommended and may become obligatory for those who fear falling into sin.
summary.explanation: Marriage is encouraged in Islam and protects chastity, with its ruling varying according to a person's circumstances.

summary.questionText: List the main pillars or conditions of a valid Islamic marriage.
summary.correctAnswer: Consent of both parties, a guardian (wali), at least two witnesses, the mahr (dowry), and a clear offer (ijab) and acceptance (qabul).
summary.explanation: These elements together make the nikah valid and protect the rights of both husband and wife.

summary.questionText: Mention three purposes of marriage in Islam.
summary.correctAnswer: To gain tranquillity, love and mercy between spouses; to continue the human race through lawful children; and to protect chastity and avoid sin.
summary.explanation: Marriage fulfils emotional, social and moral aims in the believer's life.

summary.questionText: State two rights of the wife upon her husband.
summary.correctAnswer: The right to the mahr and the right to maintenance (nafaqah) such as food, clothing and shelter, as well as kind and just treatment.
summary.explanation: Islam guarantees the wife both financial support and respectful treatment from her husband.

summary.questionText: State two responsibilities of the wife in the family.
summary.correctAnswer: To care for the home and children, and to be loyal, respectful and cooperative with her husband within the bounds of Islam.
summary.explanation: The wife shares in building a stable, loving home and raising upright children.

summary.questionText: Who are the mahram relations a man may not marry?
summary.correctAnswer: Close relatives such as his mother, daughter, sister, aunts and nieces, as well as certain relatives through marriage and breastfeeding.
summary.explanation: These relationships are permanently forbidden for marriage in order to protect family ties and honour.

summary.questionText: Explain the condition that governs polygyny in Islam.
summary.correctAnswer: A man may marry up to four wives only if he is able to treat them all with justice and equality; if he fears he cannot, he should marry only one.
summary.explanation: Justice is the central requirement, and the Qur'an warns those who cannot be fair to limit themselves to one wife.

summary.questionText: Why is divorce considered a last resort in Islam?
summary.correctAnswer: Because, although lawful, divorce is the most disliked of permitted things to Allah; it breaks up the family, so reconciliation and patience are encouraged first.
summary.explanation: Islam values preserving the family and only permits divorce when reconciliation has genuinely failed.

summary.questionText: What is the purpose of the iddah after divorce?
summary.correctAnswer: It is a waiting period that confirms whether the woman is pregnant, protects lineage, and allows time for possible reconciliation before remarriage.
summary.explanation: The iddah safeguards the rights of the child and gives the couple a final chance to reunite.

hoq.questionText: A man wishes to marry a woman, but her father refuses without any valid reason while she and the man are both willing and suitable. According to mainstream Sunni teaching, what is the best Islamic course of action?

options.text: They should marry secretly without any guardian or witnesses
The matter may be referred to another eligible guardian or an Islamic authority (such as a judge), who can act as wali if the refusal is unjust
The woman must give up the idea of marriage entirely
The man should simply take her as a wife without any contract

hoq.explanation: When a guardian unjustly withholds consent, Islam allows the matter to pass to the next eligible guardian or to an Islamic judge who can act as wali, ensuring the woman is not wronged while keeping the marriage valid and public.

hoq.questionText: A husband, in a moment of anger, wants to divorce his wife immediately. His family advises patience. What does Islamic teaching most strongly recommend in this situation?

options.text: He should divorce her at once before he calms down
He should remain calm, seek reconciliation and arbitration, and avoid hasty divorce since it is the most disliked permitted act
He should leave the home permanently without speaking
He should publicly announce her faults to the community

hoq.explanation: Islam discourages hasty divorce, especially in anger; it urges patience, reconciliation and family arbitration, reflecting the teaching that divorce is the most disliked of lawful things.

hoq.questionText: A man with two wives consistently spends more time, money and attention on the second wife while neglecting the first. How should this be judged in light of the condition for polygyny?

options.text: It is acceptable because a man may favour whichever wife he prefers
It violates the Islamic condition of justice, since a man with more than one wife must treat them fairly and equally
It is only a problem if the first wife complains to a judge
It is required that he favour the newer wife

hoq.explanation: Polygyny is permitted only on the condition of justice; deliberately neglecting one wife in time, maintenance and treatment breaks this condition and is a serious wrong in Islam.
